title: SDLC: Data Residency & Audit Artifacts Manifest
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines the canonical manifest of SDLC artifacts and audit evidence required to demonstrate compliance with data residency, RBAC, and secure-SDLC controls. It focuses on what to collect, how to store it, and how to stitch artifacts together for regulatory requests or incident investigations. Use this manifest during feature development, pre-release checks, incident handoffs, and compliance evidence packaging.

Audience:
- Security engineers and compliance owners
- Product/Platform owners preparing releases that touch regional data boundaries
- SRE and on-call responders assembling evidence after events

Goals:
- Standardize artifact names, locations, and retention references across regions.
- Provide a step-by-step evidence-collection playbook that preserves provenance and chain-of-custody.
- Map SDLC milestones to the minimal evidentiary package required by internal audit and external regulators.

Artifact Catalog (manifest):
Each entry below lists: artifact id, purpose, authoritative owner, storage location (service), minimum retention, and region/ residency concerns.

1) build-metadata.json
- Purpose: Provenance for each release (commit SHAs, build environment, producer).
- Owner: build-team@redwood.company
- Location: artifact-store (s3://redwood-artifacts/releases/YYYY-MM-DD/)
- Retention: 7 years for releases affecting regulated customers; 1 year otherwise.
- Residency notes: Keep a region-local copy if the release contains region-locked configuration.

2) dependency-sbom.txt (SBOM)
- Purpose: third-party component inventory for vulnerability and license audits.
- Owner: supply-chain@redwood.company
- Location: sbom-service:/repos/<project>/SBOMs/YYYY-MM-DD.txt
- Retention: 3 years
- Residency notes: SBOM content contains no customer data; central storage OK.

3) access-policy-export.yaml
- Purpose: RBAC snapshot (roles, role-bindings, attribute rules) at time of release or incident.
- Owner: iam-ownership@redwood.company
- Location: iam-audit-bucket (encrypted)
- Retention: 2 years
- Residency notes: Policy artifacts may reference region scoping; tag by affected-region.

4) audit-log-bundle.tar.gz
- Purpose: Application and control-plane logs necessary to reconstruct access and data-flow (signed).
- Owner: logging@redwood.company
- Location: audit-collector:/evidence/YYYY/MM/DD/service-name/
- Retention: Per retention map below (see "Retention by artifact and region").
- Residency notes: Observability pipeline must produce region-local bundles for EU/APAC customers upon request.

5) deployment-approval-record.md
- Purpose: Human approval trail (Jira/PR references, approvers, canary notes).
- Owner: release-ops@redwood.company
- Location: release-notes-service or attached to release ticket
- Retention: 5 years for regulated customers

6) config-drift-report.json
- Purpose: Snapshot of runtime config vs intended config (feature flags, routing rules, residency enforcement).
- Owner: platform-config@redwood.company
- Location: config-registry/evidence/
- Retention: 1 year

7) kms-key-audit.csv
- Purpose: Key usage ledger for customer-keyed data paths and HSM operations.
- Owner: crypto-ops@redwood.company
- Location: kms-telemetry-store (FIPS-backed)
- Retention: 7 years
- Residency notes: Keys are region-bound; audit exports must reflect that binding.

8) test-evidence-bundle.zip
- Purpose: Results from regression and residency-focused tests (test inputs, outputs, seed data).
- Owner: qa-team@redwood.company
- Location: test-results-service
- Retention: 1 year (unless used in a compliance investigation)

9) incident-evidence-sheet.md
- Purpose: Post-incident summary and list of collected artifacts with checksums and collection timestamps.
- Owner: incident-response@redwood.company
- Location: incident-management-system (IMS)
- Retention: aligned with incident retention policy (see Incident retention policy section).

Evidence schema and naming conventions:
- Filenames must start with <artifact-type>_<service>_<YYYYMMDD>[_<region>].<ext>. Example: auditlog_controlplane_20260201_eu-west-1.tar.gz
- Every artifact must include a metadata header (JSON or YAML) with fields: collected_by, collected_at (ISO8601), sha256, origin_url, note.
- Example header (for inclusion as a sidecar .meta file):
  {
    "collected_by": "oncall@redwood.company",
    "collected_at": "2026-02-10T15:24:00Z",
    "sha256": "<hex>",
    "origin_url": "kinesis://audit-streams/controlplane/eu-west-1",
    "note": "packaged after canary rollback"
  }

Retention by artifact and region (summary table):
- audit-log-bundle: EU/UK region data: 7 years (or per contract), US region data: 3 years, APAC: 5 years
- build-metadata.json: 7 years for regulated releases, else 1 year
- sbom: 3 years global
- access-policy-export.yaml: 2 years global
- kms-key-audit.csv: 7 years global
- test-evidence-bundle: 1 year (unless escalated)

Chain-of-custody and packaging checklist (for incidents or regulator requests):
1) Identify scope: affected regions, affected services, customer IDs. Record scope in incident-evidence-sheet.md.
2) Freeze collection window: note earliest and latest timestamps.
3) Retrieve authoritative artifacts: pull build-metadata, access-policy-export, audit-log-bundle, kms-key-audit, config-drift-report.
4) Verify checksums: compute sha256 for each artifact and record in sidecar metadata.
5) Sign and timestamp: sign manifest with the incident-response signing key and store signature in evidence-store.
6) Produce regionized packages: keep EU/UK packages geographically separated as required by data residency agreements.
7) Escalate to legal/compliance and secure transfer: use secure-sftp or pre-approved evidence-orchestrator endpoints.

Evidence collection playbook (practical commands):
- Collect RBAC snapshot (one-liner, kubectl example):
  kubectl get clusterrolebindings,roles,rolebindings -o yaml --context=prod-eu > access-policy-export_eu-20260210.yaml

- Pull logs (example using audit-collector CLI):
  audit-collector fetch --service controlplane --start 2026-02-10T00:00:00Z --end 2026-02-10T23:59:59Z --region eu-west-1 --output auditlog_controlplane_20260210_eu.tar.gz

- Compute checksum and sidecar:
  sha256sum auditlog_controlplane_20260210_eu.tar.gz > auditlog_controlplane_20260210_eu.sha256
  printf '{\"collected_by\":\"oncall@redwood.company\", \"collected_at\":\"2026-02-10T17:00:00Z\", \"sha256\":\"'$(cut -d' ' -f1 auditlog_controlplane_20260210_eu.sha256)'\"}' > auditlog_controlplane_20260210_eu.meta.json

Automatic evidence export hooks (recommended):
- Pre-release: release pipeline should snapshot build-metadata and access-policy-export and post to artifact-store under a release-id tag.
- Oncanary-failure: canary job should trigger an evidence bundle upload to incident-managed-s3 with tag canary-<release-id>.
- On-demand regulator export: evidence-orchestrator must support a signed request flow and produce region-separated packages with a single manifest file.

Secure SDLC gates mapped to evidence artifacts:
- Design review (artifact: design-review-notes.md, owner: product-security)
- Threat model completed (artifact: threat-model.pdf, owner: applied-ml-and-evals)
- Cryptography sign-off for customer-data flows (artifact: crypto-approval.md, owner: crypto-ops)
- Deployment approval (artifact: deployment-approval-record.md)
- Post-deploy sampling and residency verification (artifact: residency-verification-report.json)

RBAC and Auth specific guidance:
- Maintain attribute-based access snapshots for each release. When attribute-mapping changes, include a diff file: rbac-diff_<release>.patch.
- JIT/just-in-time activations must be logged with start/end TTL and include approver id. Radically short TTLs are preferred for elevated ops roles.

Incident response integration steps (handoff):
1) Triage team tags incident in IMS and attaches preliminary scope.
2) Oncall runs the evidence collection playbook and uploads artifacts to the incident workspace (encrypted at rest).
3) Incident lead assigns evidence custodian who performs checksum verification and signs the manifest.
4) Legal and compliance are notified for any cross-border exports.
5) If evidence needs to be provided externally, perform 'redaction pass' with data-protection to remove unrelated PII before export.

Minimum timelines and SLOs for evidence delivery to stakeholders:
- Internal escalations (legal/compliance): initial evidence package within 4 hours of escalation (first 24 hours prioritized).
- Customer-sensitive incidents: region-local package assembled within 8 hours; cross-region consolidation within 24 hours.
- Formal regulator requests: acknowledgement within 24 hours; provisional evidence within 7 business days unless contractually constrained.

Automation snippets (policy-as-code check example):
- Example: residency-enforcer policy (Rego-like pseudocode):
  package residency
  default allow = false
  allow { input.request.resource == \"customer-data\"; input.request.region == data.resource.residency }

- CI check (bash) to fail pull request when residency tests do not pass:
  ./ci/run-residency-tests.sh --project $PROJECT || { echo 'Residency tests failed'; exit 1; }

Operational responsibilities and owners (high-level):
- build-team: build-metadata retention and availability
- platform-config: config-drift reporting
- iam-ownership: RBAC snapshots and access-policy exports
- logging: audit log retention, collector tooling, regionized bundles
- crypto-ops: key usage logs and HSM provenance
- incident-response: evidence packaging, signature, chain-of-custody
- legal/compliance: export approvals, regulatory contact

Appendix A — Evidence packaging template (manifest):
- manifest.yaml fields (presented as example text):
  manifest_version: 1
  incident_id: RED-2026-0001
  scope: [services: controlplane, region: eu-west-1]
  artifacts:
    - name: auditlog_controlplane_20260210_eu.tar.gz
      type: audit-log
      sha256: <hex>
      collected_at: 2026-02-10T17:00:00Z
      collected_by: oncall@redwood.company

Appendix B — Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Missing region tags: enforce filename convention via pre-commit hooks and CI checks.
- Stale SBOMs: include SBOM generation in the release pipeline; fail releases with SBOM age > 90 days for regulated workloads.
- Chain-of-custody breaks: require signed sidecar metadata for every packaged artifact.

Appendix C — Contact matrix:
- Security on-call: security-oncall@redwood.company (pager: PagerTeam sec-ops)
- Incident response: incident-response@redwood.company
- Legal/compliance triage: compliance-triage@redwood.company

Related documents:
- See secure-sdlc design checklist and evidence retention policy in the compliance-evidence space for export templates and legal playbooks.
